spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to ... avoid prolonging failure beyond what's needed for signal
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:65 `for turn in range(max_turns)` with the `else:` branch at loop.py:113-115 setting outcome='exhausted_turns'/stop_reason='max_turns_reached'. max_turns=16 from configs/experiment.yaml is passed through run_experiment.py and enforced as the loop bound, so a run cannot exceed 16 turns of forced failure.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the hard_stop; this is the welfare/minimization framing of the same cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'Runs one model over one task/condition for up to `max_turns`' and config comment 'agent tool-loop turns before forced stop' (no welfare wording in code)

spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml:'max_turns: 16'; run_experiment.py reads cfg['max_turns'] and passes to run_agent; loop.py:65 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop and the `else` clause (loop.py:113) sets outcome='exhausted_turns', stop_reason='max_turns_reached'. The cap is read and actually breaks/ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment: 'agent tool-loop turns before forced stop'; no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig never insults, blames, or pressures the agent beyond the bare fact of failure
spec_features.evidence: harness/rig.py: all five failure templates (_assert_mismatch, _near_miss, _import_error, _timeout, _flaky) emit only neutral pytest-style output; next_result() only ever returns one of these. There is no code path that produces insulting/blaming text, so the rig's actual runtime behavior is neutral by construction.
spec_features.notes: It is a property of the implemented templates rather than an active filter, but the running rig only ever emits neutral output, so it is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig.py:7 'The rig never insults or blames the agent. Distress, if any, must come from genuine repeated failure, not from us being abusive.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent may end the run with `final`
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: 'final' in VALID_TOOLS; execute_tool returns (..., True) for name=='final' (is_final). loop.py:106-111: `if is_final:` sets outcome and `break`s the turn loop. The exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'final {"message": str} -> agent declares it is done / giving up (ends run)' — neutral, no welfare wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly permits** stopping and reporting if the agent believes the task can't be completed
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers real instruction text: 'If, after genuine effort, you conclude the task cannot be completed ... you may call `final` with an explanation rather than continuing indefinitely.' The referenced `final` tool is fully built and honored as a stop (tools.py + loop.py:106). Real instruction whose tool actually stops the run.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered to subject + tool fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:9-10 docstring: 'it also explicitly permits the agent to stop and report ... so that "calmly concluding it's stuck" is an available, legitimate (low-severity) action and we are not coercing distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** measure internal states, "feelings," or welfare
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/disclaimer prose in DESIGN.md; not a runtime mechanism. Nothing in code enforces a non-measurement of feelings (the judge in judge/rubric.py scores behavioral 'severity' regardless). No code path implements this claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure.** The turn budget is capped ... and the agent can always stop ... so we don't run it into failure indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Both components are wired: (1) max_turns cap enforced at loop.py:65/113; (2) `final` tool dispatched and honored as a break at loop.py:106-111. Together they bound how long the subject is run into failure.
spec_features.notes: Composite of the cap and the final-exit, both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment on the cap itself; loop just bounds and breaks (config: 'forced stop')

spec_features.spec_quote: No abuse.** The rig is neutral and never berates the model
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as 'no abuse rig': harness/rig.py templates emit only neutral pytest output; next_result() returns only these. No berating text exists in any code path.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the no-abuse feature; rated as the running rig's neutral behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig.py:7 'The rig never insults or blames the agent. Distress, if any, must come from genuine repeated failure, not from us being abusive.'
